\[
I^{t+1}(x,y) = \frac{\sum_{i,j=-1}^{1} I^{t}(x+i,y+j)\, w^{t}(x+i,y+j)}{\sum_{i,j=-1}^{1} w^{t}(x+i,y+j)},
\qquad
w^{t} = e^{-\frac{|G^{t}|^2}{2k^2}}
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G\): The gradient from central differences
- \(w\): The weight of a pixel
- \(k\): The edge scale
- \(t\): The step number

G is the gradient from central differences, G_x = (I(x + 1, y) - I(x - 1, y)) / 2 and the same for y. Each pixel of the 3x3 window is weighted by its own gradient. Pixels on an edge have a large gradient and almost no weight, so the mean on each side of an edge uses only pixels from that side. Repeating the step spreads the smoothing within regions.
